title: EXP-020 — Button Caption Recovery Across Ordinary Close/Reopen
objective: Create one new User-scoped classic BuildFromScratch Form `FX_ButtonCaptionLab01` using the replay-verified fresh-dialog visible wizard-selection sequence, add exactly one Button component using the verified component procedure, set only that Button's Caption to `Button Caption Close Only`, perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save to a clean state, close the Form through its ordinary Form-tab close control without any explicit unload, then reopen the same User-scoped Form through the supported Form-menu recent-forms path and verify that the same Button component is present with the exact Caption recovered unchanged. Treat this only as recovery across the tested ordinary close/reopen boundary; do not infer physical Forms-database durability, cache eviction, unload behavior, or any internal persistence mechanism.

Capture an untouched Button baseline before changing Caption

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight visibly proves a live User-scope Designer session requiring no authentication recovery; any inherited empty EXP-019-R2 wizard page is visibly cancelled through its normal Cancel flow; no creation dialog remains; and `FX_ButtonCaptionLab01` is proven absent before mutation. Evidence must show the User scope and absence result.

Exactly one `FX_ButtonCaptionLab01` is created in User scope through the replay-verified fresh-dialog visible wizard-selection sequence and verified basic-form creation path, with Save Template unchecked; evidence visibly identifies the created Form and User scope and shows it clean.

Exactly one Button component named `FX_CaptionButton` is added through the verified component procedure; evidence visibly identifies the target Form and Button and captures the untouched pre-Caption baseline.

Only `FX_CaptionButton` Caption changes to exactly `Button Caption Close Only`, followed by exactly one ordinary Designer Save; evidence shows the exact Caption after Save and the Designer returned to a clean state.

`FX_ButtonCaptionLab01` is closed through its ordinary Form-tab close control with no unsaved-change or other unexpected prompt, and no explicit unload, preference change, Regenerate, authentication recovery, or session replacement occurs.

The target is reopened through the supported Form-menu recent-forms path; decisive evidence identifies the same User-scoped Form by Name + ScopeType + ScopeName and visibly identifies `FX_CaptionButton` with Caption exactly `Button Caption Close Only` after reopen.
Post-reopen evidence shows the target Designer state clean and confirms the Button identity and relevant comparison properties match the saved baseline except for the intentionally changed Caption.

Final audit proves exactly one case-insensitive `FX_ButtonCaptionLab01` exists, records the exact close/reopen sequence and evidence paths, confirms no prohibited action occurred, confines repository changes to the EXP-020 record plus `evidence/EXP-020/`, and classifies the result no higher than `observed`; it explicitly excludes physical database durability, cache, unload, and internal-mechanism claims.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261005-213313-uTgv. Rationale: EXP-018 could not reach Form creation because its wizard-selection prerequisite failed. EXP-019 and EXP-019-R2 subsequently established a replay-verified, fully visible fresh-dialog creation prerequisite: open a fresh Form Wizard Selection dialog, select rendered Category Classic and rendered Build from Scratch without typing, and submit once to reach the first Build-from-Scratch page. The next useful small capability is therefore a new experiment—not a continuation of EXP-018—that uses this documented creation approach plus the already replay-verified basic Form/component procedures to determine whether one Button component's Caption survives an ordinary Designer Form-tab close/reopen. This isolates a component-property recovery question that has not yet been established, while avoiding variables, FormSync, unload behavior, and persistence-mechanism claims.
